verified_matches.title: The New York Herald
verified_matches.what_it_says: A post-Antietam casualty list under the heading 'Thirty-fourth New York Volunteers,' Company D. Henry Hubbell ('HenHubbell' in OCR) appears in the Co. D casualty list among the unaccounted — read as MISSING on the page image (OCR ambiguously placed it in the Wounded run; the page image governs). He is NOT listed as killed.
verified_matches.why_confirmed: The entire Co. D casualty list around his name is independently verified against the 34th NY roster + Chapin: John Green (Co. D, wounded Antietam) listed immediately before him; Peter Jolly (Co. D, killed) after him; Patrick Coonan, John Mycue, Dennis Hayes (all Co. D, in Chapin's Antietam killed list) in the Killed run; Sgt Robert McDonald (Co. D) among Wounded. This is unambiguously the 34th NY Company D casualty list, and Hubbell is in it. Identity confirmed (C1 via the company-list context + C2 date).
verified_matches.significance: This is the CLOSEST-TO-REAL-TIME documentary trace of Henry — 8 days after the battle. It captures him in limbo: reported missing, not yet killed. See DSC-2026-06-06-001.
verified_matches.ocr_caveat: OCR heavily garbled ('HenHubbell' jammed; column separators rendered as '?'). The killed/wounded/missing column boundary is OCR-fuzzy; the user's reading of the page image (MISSING) is authoritative over OCR.

notes: Upgraded from 'possible' to 'confirmed' on 2026-06-06 after the full Co. D casualty list was read and every surrounding name verified against the roster. One verified contemporary newspaper attestation of Henry.
